children: Rocket Lab Corporation (NASDAQ:RKLB) is accelerating toward mid‑2027 with equity and amended financing to fund its Iridium acquisition while advancing Neutron tests, booking missions through 2029, growing revenue/backlog and launch cadence, winning major Space Force and Viasat contracts amid mixed stock moves.
Previous Week Recap
Rocket Lab Equity Financing For Iridium
: Rocket Lab (RKLB) raised equity and secured amended financing to replace a planned bridge facility, funding the cash portion and expenses of its planned acquisition of Iridium, expected mid‑2027.
Neutron Progress Updates, Bookings Through 2029

: Rocket Lab (RKLB) updates Neutron progress: reusable fairing finished pre‑flight testing, a 10‑m second‑stage test stand was installed at LC‑3, and multiple Neutron missions are booked through 2029.
Space Force Multi-Launch Deal
: Rocket Lab (RKLB) won a $266M Space Force multi-launch deal in July 2026 for 12 suborbital launches, plus up to six optional flights, primarily from Pacific Spaceport Complex, Kodiak, Alaska.
Backlog Surges, Revenue Growth
: Rocket Lab (RKLB) Q2: backlog >$2.3B, revenue +60%+, rising Electron launches, improving margins and higher launch cadence noted, trends cited toward profitability
96th Electron Launch Milestone
: Rocket Lab (RKLB) completed its 96th Electron launch Sept 19, 2026, placing Synspective’s 12th StriX SAR at 572 km. A 97th Electron launch is scheduled within the week to 559 km.
Viasat GEO Bus Contract
: Rocket Lab (RKLB) won a Viasat contract to build a GEO satellite bus for the Protected Tactical SATCOM–Global program and joined the U.S. Space Force’s Space Data Network Consortium.
Intraday Moves On Financing/Acquisition
: RKLB swung intraday after financing and an acquisition: one report showed a ~5.3% dip to $64.22, another noted a ~2% rise on a separate day despite weaker markets.
Raymond James Initiates Coverage
: Raymond James started coverage of Rocket Lab (RKLB), assigning a Buy/Outperform rating and an $80 price target, per analyst Brian Gesuale.
Thrust Module, Integrated Testing
: Rocket Lab (RKLB) will test a thrust module on the launch mount to verify rocket-to-mount interfaces, then proceed to integrated testing, a wet dress rehearsal and a first-stage static fire.
Premarket Drop On NASA Protest

: Rocket Lab Corporation (RKLB) shares dropped in premarket trading after the company formally protested NASA’s decision to award Blue Origin the $700 million Mars Telecommunications Network contract.
